conventions.convention: The prescribed background is smooth and time-oriented, with signature (-,+,+,+). Proper-time worldlines are C² and future timelike, with U=dz/dτ and g(U,U)=-c². Mass m>0 and charge q are constant.

F is a prescribed C¹ alternating two-form. On a potential domain A is C² and F_ab=∂_a A_b−∂_b A_a. The raising operator satisfies g(F♯(v),w)=F(w,v). In the flat SI chart x⁰=ct, F_0i=−E_i/c and F_ij=ε_ijk B_k.

The adopted action is −mc∫√(−g(γ′,γ′))dλ+q∫A(γ′)dλ. Stationarity tests local C² fixed-endpoint variations through future-timelike curves; varied curves need not remain proper-time normalized. Admissible parameter changes are C² orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms with strictly positive derivative, applied to the whole variation family.
Countable Choice is assumed for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure. No full Axiom of Choice or global potential is assumed.
For χ∈C³, the gauge change is A↦A+dχ. The kinetic covector is p=mU♭; the local canonical covector is π_A=p+qA and changes by q dχ.

Spin is a classical C¹ tangent vector along the worldline, with angular-momentum units and g(s,U)=0. The dimensionless parameter g_s defines μ=(g_s q/2m)s. With G=g_s/2 and K=F(s,U), the adopted transport is Dτs=(q/m)[G F♯(s)−(G−1)UK/c²]. Its curved and varying-field versions are separate model assumptions.

The charged action describes a test body with prescribed metric and external field. It excludes self-field evaluation, self-gravity, radiation reaction, variable mass or charge, electric-dipole forces, and spin-dependent translational forces.

load_bearing.statement: On a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, assuming Countable Choice, for a C² potential on an open domain and a finite C² future-timelike proper-time segment, the fixed-endpoint first variation is δS=∫[−m g(J,∇_U U)+qF(J,U)]dτ. Stationarity under all local chart-supported variations is equivalent to m∇_U U=qF♯(U).

Defines constant positive mass, fixed charge, proper-time four-velocity, kinetic momentum P=mU, orthogonal classical polarization, magnetic moment μ=(g_s q/2m)s, and a prescribed external two-form with local potential, under the stated SI conventions and test-body exclusions.

For finite fixed-endpoint future-timelike segments in a local potential domain, the physical trajectories of the idealized model are stationary points of S[γ]=−mc∫√(−g(γ′,γ′))dλ+q∫A(γ′)dλ under the specified local C² variations.

Under the charged-body definitions, local potential domain, adopted action, stated field convention and Countable Choice, a finite C² future-timelike proper-time segment is stationary if and only if m∇_U U=qF♯(U).

For a prescribed C¹ alternating two-form on an open region of a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, assuming Countable Choice, m,c>0, real q and future initial data with g(U₀,U₀)=−c², the external Lorentz IVP has a unique local C² solution; it preserves g(U,U)=−c² and future direction.

Under the stated external-charge model and Countable Choice, every normalized future-timelike initial datum in the local potential domain has a unique local solution with g(P,P)=−m²c². In the flat inertial SI specialization, using the SR momentum result under its model assumptions, dp/dt=q(E+v×B) and dE_part/dt=qE·v.

Under its stated finite-regularity Lorentzian data and Countable Choice, for A∈C² and χ∈C³, d(A+dχ)=dA and S_(A+dχ)[z]−S_A[z]=q[χ(z(b))−χ(z(a))]. Fixed-endpoint stationarity and p=mU♭ are gauge invariant, while π_(A+dχ)=π_A+q dχ.

For the stated classical charged-body model with Lorentz-force translation, adopt Dτs=(q/m)[G F♯(s)−(G−1)UK/c²], where G=g_s/2 and K=F(s,U). Curved-background and varying-field use are independently adopted extensions.

seams_checked.note: The charge-spin definition uses the supplier's prescribed background, signature, C² worldlines, proper-time convention and distinctions among observers, charts, congruences and tetrads. It adds charged-body model data without attributing those additions to the geometry supplier.

The page and BMT constraint theorem retain the field signs, Countable Choice, local stationary-action translation and separately adopted curved BMT law. The transport formula matches because −(G−1)=1−G; no quantum or empirical conclusion is attributed to these suppliers.

Electric, magnetic and crossed-field consumers retain constant positive mass, fixed charge, flat SI conventions, Countable Choice and the action assumption. They supply smooth potentials. Their global orbit claims come from explicit orbit constructions rather than an overstatement of the local IVP supplier.

The Coulomb consumer excludes the source point, supplies a smooth potential on the remaining domain, retains Countable Choice and the flat massive-momentum assumption, and uses the supplier's orientation-preserving whole-family reparameterization result. Its scattering conclusions are restricted to the separately proved branch.

The radiation page inherits charged-body quantities and the SI tensor convention. LAD is explicitly a separate effective postulate, with stronger field and curve regularity; neither LAD nor LL is presented as a consequence of the radiation-free charged action or as a singular self-field construction.
